text:
maria: heads-up: seeing a sharp drop in local NVMe IOPS across a subset of eu-west2 hosts since 03:10 UTC, GPU provisioning failures and pending pods piling up. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/in/ops/nvme-iops?range=30m :warning:
ankit: which host pool / node ids? any SMART errors?
maria: sample nodeids: gnode-eu2-07a2, gnode-eu2-07a3, gnode-eu2-07b1. quick smartctl diff shows rising Media_Wearout and increased read-retry counts. minimal visible badblocks though.
kevin: is this after the vendor fw push last night? deploy-bot shows fw-update job finished 02:48 UTC in eu-west2.
deploy-bot: fw-rollout eu-west2 v1.2.9 -> v1.3.0 completed (02:48 UTC). changed 18 devices.
sophie: if it's FW-related we should pause any background I/O (scrubs/trims) before trying to roll back. janitor is running heavy scrubs on that pool right now.
janitor-bot: janitor-scrub started (eu-west2) window 03:00-04:00. concurrency=32.
eng-infra-oncall: please run these checks:
```
# quick NVMe health
ssh root@gnode-eu2-07a2 "nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0 | egrep 'critical_warning|media_errors|read_err|write_err|power_cycles'"
ssh root@gnode-eu2-07a2 "nvme error-log /dev/nvme0 | tail -n 30"
```
ankit: ran nvme smart-log/snips, attached core lines below:
```
critical_warning: 0
media_errors: 12
read_err: 243
write_err: 0
percent_used: 37
```
maria: also saw kernel dmesg with repeated read-retry messages and some device timeouts.
kevin: immediate mitigation: 1) pause janitor scrubs in eu-west2, 2) reduce janitor concurrency to 4, 3) mark affected nodes unsched and drain GPU pods to avoid hard failures. I'll take 1+2 now.
kevin: pausing janitor scrub for eu-west2 -> CLI:
```
# from ops control
opsctl janitor pause --region eu-west2 --reason "nvme_iops_drop"
opsctl janitor set-concurrency --region eu-west2 4
```
janitor-bot: received pause command, cancelling scheduled jobs for eu-west2 (may take 30s).
sophie: I'll start cordon/drain of the two worst nodes and shift provisioning to other zones.
sophie: cordon gnode-eu2-07a2 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data (15m ETA to reschedule pods)
ankit: needs logs for vendor escalation. please collect nvme-fw versions and full smart logs:
```
ssh root@gnode-eu2-07a2 "nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme0 | egrep 'frmw|vid|sn'"
ssh root@gnode-eu2-07a2 "nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0 > /tmp/gnode-eu2-07a2-smart.log && scp /tmp/gnode-eu2-07a2-smart.log ops@collector:/tmp/"
```
maria: collected and uploaded to /tmp/fw-collect/2901234000/ (files: gnode-eu2-07a2-fw.txt, gnode-eu2-07a3-fw.txt, gnode-eu2-07b1-fw.txt). All show v1.3.0 except one spare at v1.2.9.
kevin: vendor confirms v1.3.0 had known regression on mixed trim+scrub patterns on that controller family. They recommend rollback to v1.2.9 or apply hotfix v1.3.1 but hotfix requires per-node vendor tooling with 5-10m downtime per node.
eng-infra-oncall: proposed plan:
- step 0: keep janitor paused and restrict storage-heavy jobs in eu-west2 (NOW)
- step 1: cordon+drain affected nodes (in progress)
- step 2: schedule rolling FW rollback to v1.2.9 for the 18 impacted nodes, 1 node at a time, maintenance mode (expected 8-12m per node)
- step 3: monitor IOPS and provisioning backlog, restore janitor at reduced concurrency after first 3 nodes completed
- step 4: vendor to provide formal RCA and recommend long term patching strategy
ankit: agree. add a temporary route to failover provisioning to eu-central if queue > 100 for > 10m. opsctl route-update --prefer eu-central --threshold 100
maria: starting to move active scheduling to eu-central and us-west. provisioning timeouts reduced but still seeing queued pods for GPU lower-priority jobs. customer-facing latency: a handful of infra customers hit longer start times, ops-notification prepared.
kevin: starting rollback on gnode-eu2-07a2 (taking node offline). I'll post progress. ETA per node ~10m.
kevin: rollback complete on 07a2, IOPS recovered to baseline in ~90s. provisioning backlog dropped by 28%.
sophie: great. continuing rollouts in batches of 2 nodes to keep churn low.
eng-infra-oncall: reopening janitor in 30m with concurrency=8 after we validate steady-state post-rollbacks for first batch.
maria: vendor owes us a postmortem. please keep collecting logs and any persistent SMART counts.
ankit: grabbing logs for escalation. linking incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3389
kevin: status update in 40m.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
